<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 Balakot airstrike]]
**[[Pakistan]] reports [[India]]n military aircraft violated their airspace near [[Muzaffarabad]] and "released a payload" which landed near [[Balakot]]. After this, Pakistan [[Scrambling (military)|scrambled]] their own jets, but state no casualties or damage have been inflicted. India claims the incident was an airstrike on a [[Jaish-e-Mohammed]] camp in Balakot in retaliation to the [[Pulwama attack]] days earlier. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-kashmir-pakistan/pakistan-says-indian-aircraft-released-a-payload-after-crossing-frontier-no-casualties-idUSKCN1QF07B (Reuters)], [https://www.news18.com/news/india/india-strikes-pakistan-live-air-force-jets-cross-loc-destroy-jem-terrorist-camp-with-1000-kg-laser-guided-bombs-2048631.html (CNN-News18)]
**The attack is the first time since [[Indo-Pakistani War of 1971]] that the [[Indian Air Force]] has crossed and attacked Pakistan beyond the [[line of control]]. As well as the first time since both countries have acquired [[nuclear weapons]]. [https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/india-airstrike-in-pakistan-iaf-crosses-loc-first-time-since-1971-war-1465178-2019-02-26 (India Today)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Two [[Long Island Rail Road]] trains collide into a car in [[Westbury, New York]], United States, killing all three occupants in the car. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/26/nyregion/lirr-train-collision-accident.html (''The New York Times'')]

;International relations
*[[Nuclear warfare]], [[Russia–United States relations]]
**Following [[Vladimir Putin]]'s warning that Russia would deploy [[Nuclear weapon|nuclear missiles]] in Europe if the United States deploys intermediate-range [[Nuclear weapon|nuclear missiles]] in Europe, Putin's ally [[Dmitry Kiselyov]] lists what he claims are the targets in the United States, which includes [[The Pentagon]], [[Camp David]], [[Fort Ritchie]], [[McClellan Air Force Base]], and [[Jim Creek Naval Radio Station]]. [[Kremlin Press Secretary|Kremlin spokesperson]] [[Dmitry Peskov]] denies the existence of the target list. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-nuclear-russia/after-putins-warning-russian-tv-lists-nuclear-targets-in-u-s-idUSKCN1QE1DM (Reuters)], [http://tass.com/politics/1046259 (TASS)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]], [[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**Two [[United States Armed Forces|United States military]] officials tell CNN that the U.S. military has flown [[reconnaissance]] flights in international [[Airspace|airspace]] off the coast of Venezuela during the last several days to gather classified intelligence about President [[Nicolás Maduro]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/25/americas/venezuela-developments/index.html (CNN)]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] imposes sanctions on governors of four [[States of Venezuela|states of Venezuela]], all of them members of the ruling [[United Socialist Party of Venezuela|United Socialist Party]]. [https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm616 (United States Department of the Treasury)]
**[[Migración Colombia|Colombia's Immigration Agency]] says 274 [[Military personnel|military personnel]] from different branches of the [[National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela|Venezuela's Armed Forces]], [[Venezuelan National Police|Venezuela's National Police]], and [[Venezuelan National Guard|Venezuela's National Guard]] have defected to Colombia. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/25/americas/venezuela-developments/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2019 North Korea–United States Hanoi Summit]]
**[[List of leaders of North Korea|North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] visits his country's embassy in [[Hanoi]] on Tuesday in preparation for the summit. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-usa-kim-outing/north-koreas-kim-begins-hanoi-trip-by-visiting-embassy-idUSKCN1QF15U (Reuters)]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] lands in Vietnam's capital for the summit. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/trump-arrives-in-vietnam-for-second-summit-with-north-korean-leader-11551190215 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Australia]], [[Pope Francis#Sexual abuse|Pope Francis's response to sexual abuse in the Catholic Church]]
**Australian [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|cardinal]] [[George Pell]] is convicted of [[Sexual assault|sexually assaulting]] two 13-year-old choirboys at [[St Patrick's Cathedral, Melbourne|Melbourne’s St Patrick’s Cathedral]].  The verdict has been suppressed by a [[Gag order|gag order]] until now. He is the [[Catholic Church]]'s most senior official to be convicted of a sexual crime in history. [https://www.theage.com.au/national/victoria/cardinal-george-pell-found-guilty-of-child-sex-abuse-20181214-p50m86.html (The Age)] [https://www.theage.com.au/national/victoria/george-pell-guilty-verdict-fallout-live-20190226-p510ao.html (The Age<sub>2</sub>)]
*[[Terrorism in Israel]]
**A [[Jew]]ish [[Israel]]i teen is convicted of membership of a terror organisation, arson, and racially aggravated assault. He is the second Jewish person convicted of terror group membership ever in Israel in connection to crimes against [[palestinian people|Palestinians]]. His conviction was announced today, but occurred last week in secrecy. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/settler-teen-convicted-of-terror-offenses-for-attacks-on-palestinians/ (The Times of Israel)]
;Politics and elections
*[[Trump administration family separation policy]]
**An oversight committee is expected to vote on whether to subpoena [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] officials over family separations at the southern border. [https://www.apnews.com/0b012aaaa6454a10a585eb4a848c8541 (AP News)]
*[[2019 Nigerian general election]]
**[[Nigeria]] reelects President [[Muhammadu Buhari]]. [http://www.africanews.com/2019/02/27/buhari-beats-atiku-to-secure-re-election-as-nigeria-president/ (Africa News)]
